checklist.notes: Four activities address sequencing, information focus, or integrated prior help language, but the speaking item is tagged for narrative sequence while asking only for request acceptance and an object quantity.
The reading, completion, focus matching, and translation tasks provide clear practice; the speaking rubric also supports a bounded response.
The set moves from comprehension and controlled form/focus work to speaking and translation with manageable transitions.
Individual instructions are understandable and output limits are explicit.
Short texts and one- or two-sentence production keep demands manageable.
Vietnamese translation, familiar names, and concrete helping contexts are relevant without stereotyping learners.
Five short activities are proportionate for A2.2.

methods: Reviewed the exercise set and audit against the declared original project-authored policy and external-payload/media declarations.

findings.description: ex_A2-U04-L02_004 declares concept_narrative_sequence as its target, but its prompt and rubric assess accepting a request and emphasizing “two folders”; no event sequence is elicited or assessed.
findings.recommendation: Redesign the task to require an ordered sequence of helping events, or bind it only to the interaction and sentence-focus objectives actually assessed.

limitations: This is an independent AI pedagogical review for development evidence, not human review or release approval.
The review covers the supplied immutable exercise set and automated audit; it does not report an Internet-wide originality search.
